title: Caffeine shift scratch - Nisha
content:
04/18 shift notes (coffee-fueled, messy)

00:18 - woke to pager (pager duty). page: infra-api-5xx-alert (paginated).
  - source: api-gateway -> 503 from model-proxy-01 cluster (eu-west-1).
  - initial action: scaled proxy pool (kubectl scale deployment model-proxy --replicas=6 -n prod-eu) to reduce queuing.
  - quick check: node metrics looked ok, CPU ~65%, mem ~72%. network latencies spiked.
  - mitigation: enabled fallback routing to dedicated-fallback (policy=region-fallback) for high-latency requests.
  - outcome: 503s dropped from 140/min -> 12/min over 11m.

01:04 - follow-up triage notes:
  - suspected root cause: intermittent connection resets between proxy and model runtime (tcp RSTs). Logs show repeated "connection reset by peer" from runtime container (model-runtime-v2).
  - correlate: see SRE-7892 (ticket) where Mateo observed similar resets last month after kernel update on dedicated nodes. possible pattern.
  - temp workaround: pin runtime image to v2.3.1 on eu cluster and restart subset (canary) before rolling update.

Immediate TODOS (short):
  [ ] confirm if kernel patch rolled on eu fleet last night (ask infra on-call)
  [ ] pin model-runtime image to v2.3.1 on prod-eu canary (kubectl set image ... / monitor 10m)
  [ ] add tcp_retransmit/sec to the alert graph for proxy->runtime path (grafana: infra/proxy-runner)
  [ ] create small runbook addendum: when proxy 5xx with tcp RSTs -> fallback + scale + pin image (very short checklist)

Runbook gaps found (notes to self):
  - current runbook for "proxy 5xx" assumes CPU/mem saturation; it doesn't explicitly cover connection resets or node-level kernel regressions. need to add branching logic.
  - no playbook entry for "pin image and canary restart" — add commands and expected verification steps (curl healthz 10x across different nodes).

Longer followups (to be handed off):
  - SRE-7892: owner: Mateo (mentioned) -> add postmortem stub and link to this note.
  - Engage platform-eng to confirm kernel/security updates in eu-prod for the past 48h. owner: @Priya (assign in slack).
  - Add a synthetic test that simulates sustained small TCP resets and validate fallback path doesn't overload dedicated-fallback pool. (ticket SRE-7925?)

Commands I ran (copy-paste later):
  - kubectl get pods -n prod-eu -l app=model-proxy -o wide
  - kubectl logs model-proxy-01 -n prod-eu --since=30m | grep "connection reset" | tail -n 40
  - kubectl set image deployment/model-runtime model-runtime=redwood/model-runtime:v2.3.1 -n prod-eu --record
  - curl -sS -H "Host: api.redwood.test" https://eu.gateway.healthz || echo "health fail"

Paging timeline (quick):
  - 00:18 alert -> page to me
  - 00:20 Mateo joined, Priya pinged in slack
  - 00:27 scaled proxies, enabled fallback route
  - 00:35 canary restart of 2 runtime pods (v2.3.1)
  - 00:45 post-mitigation monitoring: error rate trending down

Notes to include in post-incident message (raw):
  - brief summary of impact (short): transient 503 spike affecting ~3% of requests in eu-west-1 for ~25m window; major customers routed correctly via fallback; no data loss.
  - root cause hypothesis: transient TCP connection resets between proxy and runtime; possible correlation with kernel updates on eu nodes.
  - actions taken: scaled proxy pool, enabled fallback routing, pinned runtime image to v2.3.1 on canary then rolled to remaining nodes after observation window.
  - next steps: confirm kernel updates, add runbook branching, add tcp metric to alert dashboards, schedule postmortem if repro found.

Random to-dos and reminders (personal):
  - send quick note to @oncall-rotation channel about shift handover (what to watch: eu proxy 5xx, pinned runtime image).
  - follow up with product about customers who reported timeouts (list from Sentry errors).
  - remind myself to hydrate.

Loose ideas (for longer-term):
  - automated canary restart action: when proxy 5xx & tcp_retransmit high -> automatically spin up canary runtime with older image and route 5% traffic for 5m; if failure drops, promote. need safety gating.
  - improved observability: distribute per-connection histograms (short-term) so we can spot increases in resets without digging logs.

End of shift handover blurb (to copy to handover doc):
  "eu-west-1: transient proxy->runtime TCP resets caused 503 spike around 00:15-00:40 UTC. Mitigation: scaled proxy, enabled region-fallback, canary pinned runtime to v2.3.1, rolled after observation. Monitoring shows error rate returned to baseline. Follow-ups: confirm kernel updates, update runbook, create synthetic test for resets. Nisha to follow up with platform-eng and coordinate postmortem if needed."

-- Nisha

(rough and messy — keep as scratchpad until I file the ticket updates and tidy up the runbook)
